sources.title: Learning from failure in health care: frequent opportunities, pervasive barriers

findings.finding: Feeling safe allows learners to stop worrying about their image and focus entirely on the learning task.
findings.quote: Students' sense of PS appeared to free them to focus on learning in the present moment without considering the consequences for their image in the eyes of others.

findings.finding: An environment that encourages provisional attempts and tolerates failure without guilt is essential for learning.
findings.quote: thus a climate is built which encourages provisional tries and which tolerates failure without retaliation, renunciation, or guilt

findings.finding: Openly discussing mistakes creates a cycle where learners feel more comfortable reporting and learning from errors in the future.
findings.quote: members in units with psychological safety discuss errors more, which leads to other members being more willing to report errors in the future as there is less risk associated with reporting mistakes.

principle: Psychological safety creates an environment where learners feel free to take risks and focus on the task at hand without fear of judgment or negative consequences for making mistakes.
for_the_teacher: Explicitly state at the beginning of the lesson that mistakes are a normal and expected part of the learning process.
Share your own past struggles or mistakes to model that it is safe to be imperfect.
Use encouraging language that focuses on the effort of trying rather than the perfection of the result.
when_it_does_not_apply: Psychological safety may not facilitate learning in environments where there is an absence of interdependence between team members.
